title: In-Memory Database (4 levels)
description_html:
Implement an in-memory database of records. Each record is a key holding several field → value pairs.

Levels

  1. Level 1: record CRUD
    • set(key, field, value), get(key, field), delete(key, field)
  2. Level 2: filtering
    • scan(key) and scan_by_prefix(key, prefix) return the matching fields, ordered, as "field(value)"
  3. Level 3: TTL
    • Every operation takes a timestamp; set can take a ttl
    • An expired field acts as if it was never set, for reads and scans alike
  4. Level 4: look-back
    • Read the database as it was at an earlier timestamp (reported variants: backup / restore to a point in time)

Constraints / rules

  • Levels 2–4 build on level 1, so keep the storage behind one class.

Progressive round: each level unlocks after the previous one passes. Write level 1 so later levels extend it rather than rewrite it.

Source: 1point3acres eBay industry coding assessment ("CRUD, filtering, TTL, look-back"); also reported for Anthropic and Meta. Candidate-reported; exact wording varies between reports.
